content: Fox-Fordyce disease is a chronic condition characterized by the obstruction of sweat gland ducts. This blockage leads to a secondary inflammatory response, which is nonbacterial in nature, caused by the accumulation of secretions and cellular debris within the cysts. While it shares similarities with hidradenitis, the latter often involves a secondary bacterial infection, resulting in the formation of pus-draining sinuses. Fox-Fordyce disease is a severe dermatological condition for which universally effective treatments are not currently available. The disease is named after George Henry Fox and John Fordyce, who contributed to its identification and understanding. The primary treatment approach involves the surgical removal of the skin tissue containing the affected sweat glands. In some cases, irradiation therapy may be employed. Antibiotics are often used to mitigate the inflammatory response associated with the condition. Fordyce granules, which are unrelated to the inflammatory process, do not require treatment unless cosmetic removal of labial lesions is desired. Inflamed glands can be managed with topical clindamycin. When the affected tissue is surgically excised, recurrence of the disease does not occur. Although exceedingly rare, neoplastic transformation of the affected glands has been documented.
